title: Anesthesia Drug Dosage Calculator
problem: Anesthesiologist Assistants must calculate precise drug dosages for induction, maintenance, and emergency medications based on patient weight, age, comorbidities, and renal/hepatic function. Manual calculation under time pressure in the OR increases risk of dosing errors, which can lead to adverse patient outcomes, malpractice claims, and regulatory action.
who: CAAs administering anesthesia in operating rooms and ambulatory surgical centers

skill_spec.name: Anesthesia Dosage Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates weight-based and adjusted dosages for common anesthesia induction, maintenance, and emergency drugs
skill_spec.formula_hint: propofol induction = 1.5-2.5 mg/kg; fentanyl = 1-2 mcg/kg; succinylcholine = 1-1.5 mg/kg; adjust for age >65 (reduce 20-30%), renal/hepatic impairment

title: IV Fluid and Blood Product Calculator
problem: CAAs must calculate intraoperative fluid requirements including maintenance fluids, deficit replacement, third-space losses, and blood product transfusion triggers. Errors in fluid management can cause hypovolemia, fluid overload, or transfusion reactions. Calculations vary by procedure type, patient weight, NPO duration, and estimated blood loss.
who: CAAs managing intraoperative fluid therapy in surgical cases

skill_spec.name: Perioperative Fluid Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates maintenance IV fluids, NPO deficit replacement, estimated blood loss replacement, and transfusion triggers
skill_spec.formula_hint: 4-2-1 rule: 4mL/kg first 10kg + 2mL/kg next 10kg + 1mL/kg remaining; NPO deficit = maintenance * NPO hours; third-space: minimal 2-4 mL/kg/hr, moderate 4-6, severe 6-8; transfusion trigger Hgb <7 g/dL

example_queries: Calculate fluid requirements for a 70 kg patient, NPO 8 hours, undergoing open abdominal surgery with EBL 500 mL

title: Pre-Operative Assessment Checklist
problem: CAAs must complete thorough pre-operative assessments covering patient history, airway evaluation, lab results, medication reconciliation, consent verification, and anesthesia machine checks. Missing any step can delay surgery, compromise patient safety, or create liability. The checklist varies by procedure type and patient risk factors.
who: CAAs performing pre-procedure patient assessments in hospitals and ASCs

skill_spec.name: Pre-Op Assessment Checklist
skill_spec.one_liner: Comprehensive pre-operative assessment checklist covering patient evaluation, equipment checks, and documentation requirements
steps: Step 1: Review patient medical history - allergies, medications, prior anesthesia reactions
Step 2: Perform airway assessment - Mallampati score, neck mobility, thyromental distance, BMI
Step 3: Review and verify laboratory results - CBC, BMP, coagulation studies, type & screen if applicable
Step 4: Medication reconciliation - NPO compliance, held medications (anticoagulants, diabetic meds), continuation meds
Step 5: Verify informed consent signed and procedure site marked
Step 6: Check anesthesia machine - pipeline pressures, vaporizer levels, circuit integrity, suction, monitors calibrated
Step 7: Prepare emergency airway equipment - backup plan (video laryngoscope, LMA, surgical airway kit)
Step 8: Confirm IV access and fluid setup
Step 9: Prepare and label all medications per ASTM standards
Step 10: Brief supervising anesthesiologist on assessment findings and anesthetic plan
Step 11: Complete time-out with surgical team
warnings: Warning: Never proceed without verified allergy status
Warning: Document Mallampati score and any anticipated difficult airway
Warning: Confirm NPO status - aspiration risk if non-compliant
regulatory_refs: ASA Practice Guidelines for Preanesthesia Evaluation

title: Malignant Hyperthermia Emergency Protocol
problem: Malignant hyperthermia (MH) is a rare but life-threatening emergency triggered by volatile anesthetics or succinylcholine. CAAs must respond within minutes with the correct sequence of interventions: stop triggering agent, administer dantrolene (dose calculation), hyperventilate, cool patient, treat hyperkalemia. Delays or wrong dosing are often fatal.
who: All CAAs administering general anesthesia with triggering agents

skill_spec.name: MH Emergency Response Protocol
skill_spec.one_liner: Step-by-step malignant hyperthermia crisis protocol with dantrolene dosing and team role assignments
steps: Step 1: STOP all triggering agents immediately (volatile anesthetics, succinylcholine)
Step 2: Call for help - activate MH hotline (1-800-644-9737) and assign team roles
Step 3: Hyperventilate with 100% O2 at high fresh gas flows (>=10 L/min)
Step 4: Administer dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg IV push, repeat every 5 min up to 10 mg/kg
Step 5: Active cooling - cold IV saline, ice packs to groin/axillae/neck, lavage if available
Step 6: Treat hyperkalemia - calcium chloride 10 mg/kg, insulin/glucose, sodium bicarbonate
Step 7: Treat arrhythmias - avoid calcium channel blockers with dantrolene
Step 8: Monitor ABGs, electrolytes, CK, myoglobin, coagulation q15 min
Step 9: Insert urinary catheter - monitor for myoglobinuria, maintain UO >2 mL/kg/hr
Step 10: Continue dantrolene 1 mg/kg q4-6h for 24-48 hours post-event
Step 11: Transfer to ICU, monitor for recrudescence for 72 hours
warnings: Warning: DO NOT use calcium channel blockers - fatal hyperkalemia with dantrolene
Warning: Each vial of dantrolene requires 60 mL sterile water - reconstitution is time-consuming, assign dedicated person
Warning: Monitor for recrudescence up to 72 hours post-event

example_queries: Walk me through the MH protocol step by step
How much dantrolene do I give for a 90 kg patient with suspected malignant hyperthermia?

title: Anesthesia Time Unit Calculator
problem: Anesthesia billing requires precise calculation of time units from anesthesia start to end, plus base units and modifying units per the ASA Relative Value Guide. Each 15-minute increment equals one time unit. Incorrect time documentation or unit calculation directly reduces reimbursement or triggers audit flags from CMS.
who: CAAs completing anesthesia records and case documentation for billing

skill_spec.name: Anesthesia Time & Billing Unit Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates total anesthesia units (base + time + modifying) and estimated reimbursement from case times
skill_spec.formula_hint: time_units = total_minutes / 15; total_units = base_units + time_units + physical_status_modifier + qualifying_circumstances; reimbursement = total_units * conversion_factor

title: Post-Anesthesia Recovery Assessment Checklist
problem: CAAs conducting post-operative rounds must systematically assess patient recovery using Aldrete scoring, check for common complications (PONV, respiratory depression, emergence delirium, hypothermia), verify pain control, and document readiness for discharge or transfer. Missed complications in PACU can result in patient harm, readmission, and liability.
who: CAAs performing post-operative patient rounds and PACU assessments

skill_spec.name: PACU Recovery Assessment Checklist
skill_spec.one_liner: Systematic post-anesthesia recovery assessment with Aldrete scoring and complication screening
steps: Step 1: Assess airway patency and oxygen saturation - SpO2 >94% on room air or baseline
Step 2: Evaluate respiratory pattern - rate, depth, adequacy of ventilation
Step 3: Check hemodynamic stability - BP within 20% of baseline, heart rate, rhythm
Step 4: Assess level of consciousness - orientation, response to commands, Aldrete score
Step 5: Evaluate pain level - numeric rating scale, assess surgical site
Step 6: Screen for PONV - administer antiemetics per protocol if needed
Step 7: Check temperature - treat hypothermia (<36°C) with forced-air warming
Step 8: Assess motor function - movement of all extremities, regional block regression
Step 9: Review IV fluids, urine output, and drainage
Step 10: Calculate total Aldrete score - discharge criteria met when score >=9
Step 11: Document assessment and communicate with PACU nursing staff
Step 12: Report significant findings to supervising anesthesiologist
warnings: Warning: Respiratory depression may occur 30-60 min after opioid administration
Warning: Do not discharge patient with Aldrete score <9 without anesthesiologist approval
Warning: Monitor regional anesthesia patients for delayed block resolution and urinary retention
regulatory_refs: CMS Conditions of Participation - Anesthesia Services

title: Anesthesia Machine Pre-Use Checkout
problem: Before every first case of the day, CAAs must perform a comprehensive anesthesia machine checkout per ASA guidelines. This includes testing pipeline and cylinder gas supplies, verifying vaporizer function, checking the breathing circuit for leaks, testing ventilator, confirming scavenging system, and calibrating monitors. Skipping steps can result in intraoperative equipment failure.
who: CAAs setting up and checking anesthesia workstations before daily cases

skill_spec.name: Anesthesia Machine Checkout Procedure
skill_spec.one_liner: Step-by-step anesthesia workstation pre-use checkout per 2008 ASA recommendations
steps: Step 1: Verify auxiliary oxygen cylinder and self-inflating manual ventilation device available
Step 2: Verify patient suction is adequate
Step 3: Turn on anesthesia delivery system and confirm AC power
Step 4: Verify pipeline gas pressures (O2 50 psi, N2O 50 psi, Air 50 psi)
Step 5: Verify backup O2 cylinder supply is adequate (>1000 psi) and turn off
Step 6: Verify correct vaporizer filling level and seated properly, filler ports closed
Step 7: Verify CO2 absorbent is adequate and not exhausted (color indicator)
Step 8: Perform breathing system pressure and leak test
Step 9: Verify gas flows through correct flowmeters - test O2 flush
Step 10: Calibrate O2 monitor and check low O2 alarm
Step 11: Verify ventilator settings and test all modes
Step 12: Check scavenging system connections and function
Step 13: Verify all monitors functional - SpO2, ETCO2, ECG, NIBP, temperature
Step 14: Set all alarms to appropriate limits
Step 15: Document checkout completion
warnings: Warning: NEVER use a machine that fails the leak test
Warning: Exhausted CO2 absorbent can cause hypercapnia - check color indicator
Warning: Test backup O2 cylinder but leave closed during case to prevent undetected pipeline failure
regulatory_refs: ASTM F1850-00 Standard for Anesthesia Workstations

example_queries: What's the correct order for anesthesia machine checkout?

title: Local Anesthetic Systemic Toxicity Calculator
problem: CAAs administering regional anesthesia must calculate maximum safe doses of local anesthetics (lidocaine, bupivacaine, ropivacaine) based on patient weight, with and without epinephrine. Exceeding maximum doses causes Local Anesthetic Systemic Toxicity (LAST) - seizures, cardiac arrest, and death. Multiple injection sites in a single case require cumulative tracking.
who: CAAs performing regional anesthesia blocks and local anesthetic administration

skill_spec.name: Local Anesthetic Max Dose & LAST Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates maximum safe local anesthetic doses by weight and tracks cumulative dosing across multiple injection sites
skill_spec.formula_hint: lidocaine max = 4.5 mg/kg (7 mg/kg with epi); bupivacaine max = 2.5 mg/kg (3 mg/kg with epi); ropivacaine max = 3 mg/kg; volume = dose / (concentration% * 10); Intralipid bolus = 1.5 mL/kg

example_queries: What's the max dose of 0.25% bupivacaine with epi for a 60 kg patient?
